newsitem.title: CHINA: Yuan ends down against US dollar in Shanghai.
newsitem.headline: Yuan ends down against US dollar in Shanghai.

text.p: The Chinese yuan closed down at 8.2922 against the U.S. dollar on Monday on profit-taking after hitting a two-year high of 8.2918 last Friday, traders said.
But the yuan is still viewed as fundamentally strong, and is expected to continue on an upward trend after a short-term technical correction, they said.
The weighted average price on Friday was 8.2918.

The yuan opened unchanged at an intraday high of 8.2918 and consolidated in a narrow range of 8.2921 and 8.2925 for most of the session, hitting a low of 8.2928. Trading was dull with most business done at 8.2924, traders said.
One dealer said the yuan faced heavy profit-taking pressure on Monday after having risen for three days in a row late last week and setting a two-year high on Friday.
"The yuan failed to hit a new high today due to profit-taking, despite strong pro-yuan sentiment," he said.
A second dealer said a technical correction was necessary before the yuan could go further.

"But given all the positive economic factors, including China's big foreign trade surplus and the continued heavy inflow of foreign investment, the yuan's upward trend will not change in the short term," he said.
Dealers said they expected the yuan to move aroud the 8.2920 level on Tuesday.

The yuan closed down at 7.1520 from 7.0978 against 100 Japanese yen on Monday due to the yen's strong performance on the world market. It closed up slightly at 1.0718 from 1.0720 against the Hong Kong dollar.
